51031249.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant human TNKS1 (1091 to 1327 residues) assessed as dissociation constant by ITC method

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Panalytical, Worcestershire, U.K.) at 25 °C. The protein (recombinant human TNKS1, residues 1091–1327) was dialyzed against 20 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, pH 7.4, and concentrated to 100 μM. The compound was dissolved in DMSO and diluted in the same buffer to a final concentration of 100 μM. The protein was loaded into the sample cell (200 μL), and the compound was loaded into the syringe (250 μL). The titration consisted of 20 injections of 2 μL each, with a spacing of 120 s between injections. The stirring speed was set to 300 rpm. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (OriginLab, Northampton, MA) with a one-site binding model. The binding affinity (Kd) was calculated from the binding isotherm. The heat of dilution was determined by titrating the compound into buffer and subtracted from the raw data. The experiments were performed in triplicate, and the results are presented as mean ± SD.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. Thermodynamic signature for the binding interaction of selected compounds with TNKS1 derived by ITC. Contributions from binding enthalpy represented by blue bars, entropic contributions represented by red bars, and over all free energy term depicted as green bar.
original_paragraph.Supporting Information S1: A detailed Watermap analysis of M2912 (30g) in complex with TNKS1 was performed (Supporting Information, Figure S1), which interestingly revealed a high energy water site at the position where the 6-methyl group is located. It was predicted that filling this water site would result in an increase of ΔG, which prompted us to investigate this by isothermal calorimetry (ITC) measurements.
